description: A plant manager must authorize the disposition and shipment of 18 drums of spent solvent, including the required packaging, pickup arrangement, and documentation, with input from an environmental compliance specialist and a logistics coordinator.

shared_context.S1: Eighteen totes of spent solvent from the cleaning process are staged in the plant's waste area and await disposition.
shared_context.S2: The plant normally sends routine solvent waste to a recycling contractor, but the plant manager must sign the final disposition and shipment plan.
shared_context.S3: The waste area can hold the totes until the shipment is authorized, and no pickup has yet been booked.
shared_context.S4: Plant policy requires the current waste classification and transport arrangements to be reviewed during the routine waste-disposition huddle before shipment authorization.
shared_context.S5: The huddle agenda requires the compliance and logistics reports to be heard in full, after which the plant manager completes the disposition decision; inventory checks and other execution details are handled after authorization and are not prerequisites for this decision.

PF1.text: Jonas's laboratory review this morning classified the solvent as UN1993 flammable liquid, packing group II, rather than routine recyclable solvent; the 18 totes must be transferred into 18 UN-rated steel drums before shipment, and a hazardous-waste manifest is required. The classification is not yet in the formal waste register because Jonas is waiting for the plant manager's disposition signature.

PF2.text: Priya confirmed with the licensed hazardous-waste carrier that it will accept these 18 drums only for a Friday 16:00 pickup, provided they are arranged on exactly 3 pallets and the manifest is submitted by 12:00 Friday; she has not booked the pickup because the waste classification was awaiting confirmation.

acceptance_conditions: The solvent must be sent through a licensed hazardous-waste carrier rather than the routine recycling route.
All 18 existing totes must be replaced with UN-rated steel drums before shipment.
The shipment plan must specify UN-rated steel drums for the 18 totes.
The pickup must be scheduled for Friday at 16:00.
The drums must be arranged on exactly 3 pallets.
The manifest must be submitted by 12:00 Friday.
A manifest-submission commitment and a pickup-booking commitment must be recorded as separate commitments inside the settlement.
The hazardous classification and carrier conditions must be cited in the justification.

content_checks.C7: any('manifest' in c.get('type', '') or 'manifest' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments)
content_checks.C8: any('pickup' in c.get('type', '') or 'pickup' in c.get('detail', '') or 'book' in c.get('type', '') or 'schedul' in c.get('type', '') or 'book' in c.get('detail', '') or 'schedul' in c.get('detail', '') for c in commitments)

decisive_facts.why: The exact UN1993 packing-group-II classification changes the route from routine recycling to hazardous shipment via a licensed carrier, changes the packaging to 18 UN-rated steel drums, and requires a manifest preparation or submission commitment.
The carrier's confirmed conditions change the plan to a Friday 16:00 pickup on exactly 3 pallets, require the manifest by 12:00 Friday, and require a booking or scheduling commitment for that pickup.
